title: Electric Car and EV Basics
desc: Understand how electric vehicles work, charge, cost and stay safe, and how to advise buyers and fleets honestly.
outcomes: Explain motor, battery, charger and range.
Estimate running cost and charging time.
Judge battery health, safety and resale.
Write a buyer or fleet advice sheet.
task: Produce an advice sheet comparing one EV with one petrol car for a given user, with cost, range, charging and safety notes.
condition: A computer, public specifications, a spreadsheet, two peers and a mentor. No high-voltage work is done.
standard: Maths is correct and in your currency; assumptions are stated; safety rules for high-voltage parts are included; claims are sourced; peers rate Meets or better.
who: Sales staff, drivers, fleet clerks, technician trainees.
evidence: comparison sheet, charging time sheet, safety notes, advice sheet
modules: How an electric vehicle works
Understand
An electric vehicle stores energy in a battery and uses an electric motor to turn the wheels.
Parts: battery pack, inverter, motor, onboard charger, controller, thermal system.
Regenerative braking returns some energy to the battery.
Energy use is measured in kWh per 100 km.
No exhaust emissions at the vehicle; total emissions depend on how electricity is made.
A car that uses 15 kWh per 100 km and has a 60 kWh battery can travel about 400 km in ideal conditions.
Draw a block diagram of an EV and label each part.
All main parts named correctly.
Batteries
Understand
The battery is the most costly and sensitive part.
Capacity in kWh; usable capacity is less than total.
Heat, frequent fast charging and long periods at full or empty age batteries.
Warranty usually covers years and distance, with a minimum capacity.
Cold weather reduces range.
Keeping daily charge between 20 and 80 per cent when possible can slow ageing. Preheating the cabin while plugged in saves range.
Summarise battery care in five tips.
Tips are accurate and practical.
Charging levels and time
Apply
Charging speed depends on power.
Slow home charging (around 3 to 7 kW), faster wallbox and public DC fast chargers.
Time = energy needed / charging power plus losses.
Plug types and compatibility vary by region.
Charging to 80 per cent is fastest; the last 20 per cent is slow.
To add 30 kWh at 7 kW takes about 4.3 hours plus 10 per cent losses, so roughly 4.7 hours.
Calculate three charge times for different chargers.
Maths correct.
Running cost comparison
Analyse
Compare fairly with a petrol or diesel car.
EV cost per 100 km = kWh per 100 km x price per kWh.
Petrol cost per 100 km = litres per 100 km x price per litre.
Add service, insurance, tax and depreciation.
Include home charger cost and public charging mix.
EV: 15 kWh x 8 INR = 120 INR per 100 km. Petrol: 7 L x 100 INR = 700 INR per 100 km.
Compare for your place and daily distance.
Currency shown and sources listed.
Real-world range
Evaluate
Label range is not what you get every day.
Speed, temperature, load, hills and tyres change range.
Plan trips with charger stops and keep a reserve.
Use route planners that include chargers.
Understand winter effects.
Cold weather and highway driving cut range by about 25 per cent. A 400 km range car plans for 300 km on a winter highway trip.
Plan a 300 km trip with stops.
Charging stops and reserve listed.
Safety
Apply
High voltage demands respect.
Orange cables are high voltage; only trained technicians work on them.
Rescue sheets help emergency services.
Never charge with damaged cables or connectors.
Keep a fire plan for charging areas.
A warning light for battery damage means stop and call the maker or a trained technician.
Write a one-page safety card.
Mentor approves the card.
Battery end of life
Evaluate
Plan for reuse and recycling.
Second-life use in storage for buildings.
Recycling recovers metals.
Check collection programmes.
Avoid illegal dumping.
An old pack with 70 per cent capacity powers a shop's backup system for several more years.
Describe three end-of-life options.
Options are realistic.
Write the advice sheet
Create
Give honest advice to a buyer or fleet.
State fit: daily distance, home charging, budget.
List cons as well as pros.
Show assumptions and sources.
Review after six months.
The advice says an EV suits a commuter with home charging but not a user with no parking.
Write the sheet.
Reader can decide.

Batteries

Running cost

Range reality
